### [2.1.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#toc)etymology

The exact name is Dangun Wanggeom ([檀](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%E6%AA%80 "檀")[](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%E7%8E%8B "王")[君王](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%E5%90%9B "君")[儉](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%E5%84%89 "儉")), but he is generally referred to as Dangun. He is affectionately called Grandpa [Dangun](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%A0%EC%95%84%EB%B2%84%EC%A7%80 "grandfather") and is a mythical figure who is said to have opened [the history](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%97%AD%EC%82%AC "history") of [Korea](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%9C%EA%B5%AD "korea") . In other words, **he is the progenitor of the Korean people** . Interpretations of the so-called Dangun myth vary depending on each person's perspective, but at least since modern times, it is common to interpret the sentences from a realistic perspective rather than the superficial story itself.

**Dangun (檀君)** is the name, and the king's name is Wanggeom. According to Professor Kim Young-ha, Dangun has the same meaning as **[Tengri](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%85%A1%EA%B7%B8%EB%A6%AC "Tengri")** in Mongolian mythology , and Wanggeom is similar to Ookimi, which means monarch in Japan.[[14]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-14 "Through this, it can be interpreted that Dangun Wanggeom has the meaning of \" the king of the sky .\"") However, Daejonggyo and others still view Dangun as the king's name and use the terms 1st Dangun and 2nd Dangun.

In the case of **Wanggeom (王儉),** there is a claim that it is a [hyangchal-](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%96%A5%EC%B0%B0 "hyangchal") style notation of 'king'. [#](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0039027 "https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0039027") In Hyangchal, when recording a two-syllable native language (ancient Korean), the first syllable would be huncha and the second syllable would be umcha, and Wang Gyeong also sees wang as hun and 儉 as yin. In this case, the original pronunciation of the first syllable must be reconstructed based on [medieval Korean](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A4%91%EC%84%B8%20%ED%95%9C%EA%B5%AD%EC%96%B4 "middle korean") . Examples include川理 ( _*NAli,_ *nari, [nae](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%82%B4#s-6 "my") ) or 國惡 ( _*NALak,_ *hell, [country](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%82%98%EB%9D%BC "country") ).[[15]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-15 "It is customary to capitalize the first syllable to indicate that it is taken from medieval Korean rather than from a recorded ancient pronunciation.") If Wang儉 was written using the same notation, the original form can be reconstructed as _*NIMkem_ and * Nimgeom based on the Middle Korean word 'Nim〯Geum〮' .If we follow the theory that王儉is the same word as [Isageum](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%B4%EC%82%AC%EA%B8%88 "moving money") , it would be _*NISkem_ and *NISkem.

If 'wanggeom' is the same as 'king', it may be a title given later. According to Chinese records of the time, the leader of Gojoseon was originally called ‘ [Hu’,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A1%B0%EC%84%A0%ED%9B%84 "After Joseon") but it was only around 323 BC that he was called ‘King’. Of course, internally he continued to be referred to as Wanggeom/Nimgeom, and King Huna may have been an external title.

### [2.2.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#toc)historical interpretation

In modern times, Dangun was highlighted as the powerful religious and political ruler of Gojoseon, led by Shin Chae-ho, and accordingly, Dangun's religion was organized into Na Cheol's Daejonggyo and played a part in [nationalism](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8C%80%EC%A2%85%EA%B5%90 "Daejonggyo") . This was designated as a national holiday by the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea and was reflected in the early days of the establishment of the modern nation, leading to Gaecheonjeol. However, [Gaecheonjeol](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B0%9C%EC%B2%9C%EC%A0%88 "National Foundation Day") was originally celebrated on October 3rd of the lunar calendar, so it was observed according to the lunar calendar even after the establishment of the Republic of Korea. In 1949, the Ministry of Education commissioned the 'Gaecheonjeol' As a result of the deliberation of the 'Solar Calendar Conversion Council', the 'National Day Act' was promulgated on October 1, 1949, based on the opinion that conversion to the yin-solar calendar was impossible and that the record of 'October 3rd' was valuable. Accordingly, the celebration was changed from October 3rd of the lunar calendar to October 3rd of the solar calendar. [#](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0001734 "https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0001734")

Modern historical circles viewed this as a product that reflected the historical beliefs of the transitional period when the northern part of the Korean peninsula and [the Manchurian](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%8C%EC%A3%BC "Manchuria") area transitioned from [the Neolithic Age](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EC%84%9D%EA%B8%B0%20%EC%8B%9C%EB%8C%80 "neolithic age") to [the Bronze Age](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%B2%AD%EB%8F%99%EA%B8%B0%20%EC%8B%9C%EB%8C%80 "bronze age") . It was interpreted as a [Bronze Age](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EC%84%9D%EA%B8%B0 "Neolithic") group with a belief in Heavenly Son was introduced into the Neolithic society of totemism, which worshiped bears and tigers, and they absorbed the tiger group and the bear group, forming the [Dangun](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B0 "bear") group [that](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%86%A0%ED%85%8C%EB%AF%B8%EC%A6%98 "totemism") later developed [into](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%98%B8%EB%9E%91%EC%9D%B4 "tiger") Gojoseon [.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%A0%EC%A1%B0%EC%84%A0 "Gojoseon") Gakjeochong Ssireumdo, a Goguryeo mural tomb from the mid-5th century, also drew attention because it had murals containing motifs from the Dangun myth. In other words, there is a mural depicting a bear and a tiger sitting with their backs to each other under a large tree with many birds sitting on it. [#](http://contents.history.go.kr/front/ht/view.do?levelId=ht_001_0020_0020 "http://contents.history.go.kr/front/ht/view.do?levelId=ht_001_0020_0020")

However, Dangun Wanggeom first appears in literature in Samgukyusa, which appeared in the late 13th century [,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%82%BC%EA%B5%AD%EC%9C%A0%EC%82%AC "Samguk Yusa") and the text Gogi (old book) that Ilyeon cited in Samgukyusa does not exist.[[16]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-16 "In fact, it is unclear whether among the books Il-yeon quoted, there is a book titled 《Gogi》, or whether it just means an old record (Gogi, Gogi). Seeing that 'Seonin Wanggeom (仙人王儉)' is mentioned as the original owner of Pyeongyang in Samguk Sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms) published in 1145, it appears that there was a mythological composition at least in the mid-Goryeo period. Since [Wanggeom](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0039027 "https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0039027") is a name referring to Dangun, it is strongly assumed that 'Seonin Wanggeom' is 'Dangun', but it is not clearly stated as Dangun. It's not even clear whether it was connected. In the Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms), the records of the late Goguryeo period were borrowed from Chinese historical records, and some monarchs, such as King Jangsu, had more records of [tributes](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A1%B0%EA%B3%B5 "tribute") than records of internal affairs, so it is not difficult to understand because records of customs are not properly preserved. However, [the pseudo-history](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9C%A0%EC%82%AC%EC%97%AD%EC%82%AC%ED%95%99 "pseudohistory") of religious groups such as [Taebaekgyo and Dandanhakhoe,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%B4%EC%9C%A0%EB%A6%BD "Lee Yoo-rip") which were created as clones of Daejonggyo in the 1970s, is problematic because it still secretly resides at [the bottom of society](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%99%98%EB%B9%A0 "Hwanpa") to this day. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Currently, the most widely known Dangun myth is from 《 **[Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%82%BC%EA%B5%AD%EC%9C%A0%EC%82%AC "Samguk Yusa")** 》, but other versions exist in various books such as 《Jewangungi》, 《The Chronicles of King Sejong》, and <Dangun Segi》. The myth of Dangun has been handed down not only in these literature records, but also in various oral literature.

Dangun is most likely a real person, but he has a strong character as a kind of mythical being, and in fact, the majority of records about him have the characteristic of having a mythical character.

[4.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#toc)Dangun faith
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

There are no records of worship for Dangun during the Three Kingdoms period or the North and South Kingdom periods. However, we can only speculate that the 'Gahan God' served in Goguryeo may be related to Dangun. Records of Dangun's ancestral rites can be found from the Goryeo Dynasty. According to the Geography of the Goryeo History, there is [Samseongsa Temple](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EC%82%AC(%EB%AC%B4%EA%B5%90) "신사(무교)") on Mt. Guwol , where Danin, Danung, and Dangun are worshiped. However, in the early and middle Goryeo Dynasty, the worship of Dangun was not that great. Samseongsa Uiju (儀注) during the 7th Mokjong period[[20]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-20 "An annotated text that recorded and annotated the rites of sacrifice.") Except for the fact that it was created, no records have been found of the government holding ancestral rites to Samseongsa Temple during the Goryeo Dynasty or of ancestral rites being held by local officials.[[21]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-21 "In Goryeosa, there is a record that the Goryeo government held a rite every season by lowering the pressure in Dongmyeongseongjesa, and Pyongyang officials held ancestral rites on the 1st and 15th of every month . You can see that it was bigger than worship.") It was during the late Goryeo Dynasty that Dangun's importance increased, and after he evacuated to Ganghwa Island during the reign of King Gojong, the remains of Ganghwa Island became known as Dangun's remains, and Dangun was elevated to the status of founder in [Jewangungi](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A0%9C%EC%99%95%EC%9A%B4%EA%B8%B0 "emperor luck") and [Samguk Yusa](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%82%BC%EA%B5%AD%EC%9C%A0%EC%82%AC "Samguk Yusa") .[[22]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-22 "This contrasts with the Samguk sagi, which was produced in the middle of the Goryeo Dynasty, which did not include the records of Dangun at all. There is a record of 'seonin wanggeom', but it is unknown whether the seonin wanggeom is Dangun.")

After the opening of the Joseon Dynasty, Taejong built a shrine in Gija in Pyongyang and enshrined Dangun in the east. King Sejong built a shrine for Dangun and King Dongmyeongseong to hold ancestral rites independently, and King Yeongjo gave the name of [Sungnyeongjeon](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%88%AD%EB%A0%B9%EC%A0%84 "Sungnyeongjeon") , which has been handed down to this day.[[23]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-23 "At this time, Kija was enshrined separately in Sunginjeon, but King Dongmyeongseong was enshrined together in Sungnyeongjeon. As Haemosu was identified with Dangun, it is assumed that King Dongmyeongseong was treated as Dangun's son.") The ancestral rites at Samseongsa were stopped with the construction of Sungnyeongjeon, but the building itself was preserved and maintained at the local level. Later, rumors circulated that the plague had spread because the ancestral rites were moved to Pyongyang, and when local public opinion intensified, it was restored during the reign of King Seongjong and has been handed down to this day.[[24]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-24 "Originally, however, mortuary tablets and wooden statues were enshrined together, but King Taejong’s great chancellor Ha Ryun suggested destroying the wooden statues enshrined in shrines across the country and enshrining only the ancestral tablets, so the wooden statues disappeared and only the ancestral tablets remained in Samseongsa. This wooden statue does not appear to have been restored.") In addition to Sungnyeongjeon Hall and Samseongsa Temple, [Chamseongdan Altar](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%B0%B8%EC%84%B1%EB%8B%A8 "Chamseongdan") on Manisan Mountain in Ganghwa-do and Dangun Tomb in Gangdong-gun, Pyongyang[[25]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-25 "During the Korean Empire, it was elevated to the Tomb of Dangun .") Dangun worship reached its heyday in [the](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8F%99%EA%B5%AD%ED%86%B5%EA%B0%90 "Dongguk Tonggam") Joseon Dynasty, with Dangun clearly appearing as the progenitor in historical records of the Joseon Dynasty, such as Dongguk Tonggam.[[26]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-26 "In addition, because Wiman was a usurper who dared to harm Dangun's legitimacy, his status fell to the bottom and he was extremely despised.")

At the end of the Joseon Dynasty , [nationalism](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%AF%BC%EC%A1%B1%EC%A3%BC%EC%9D%98 "nationalism") emerged and Dangun was very important, and furthermore, [the Daejonggyo](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8C%80%EC%A2%85%EA%B5%90 "Daejonggyo") worshiping Dangun as a god was born.[[27]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-27 "For reference, many people misunderstand, but it is Hwanin, not Dangun, who is revered as the main god in Daejonggyo .") Even in folk shamanism, Dangun was worshiped, and until now, Dangun is worshiped in the controversial [Jeungsando](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A6%9D%EC%82%B0%EB%8F%84 "transpiration") religions.

Currently, there are places related to Dangun, such as [Sungnyeongjeon](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%88%AD%EB%A0%B9%EC%A0%84 "Sungnyeongjeon") and [Dangunneung](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EB%A6%89 "Tomb of Dangun") in Pyongyang , Samseongsa Temple in Mt. Guwol, [Chamseongdan](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A7%88%EB%8B%88%EC%82%B0 "Manisan") Altar in Mt.

There is also a shrine in Japan that worships Dangun as its deity. It is located in [Kagoshima Prefecture](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B0%80%EA%B3%A0%EC%8B%9C%EB%A7%88%ED%98%84 "Kagoshima Prefecture") and is called Oksan Shrine or Tamayama Shrine. [#](https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0073540 "https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0073540") It was built by the descendants of Joseon potters who were taken away during the Imjin War. Upon visiting the site, it was located on the upper part of a cemetery that is presumed to be a family tomb on the side of a low hill. The sacred object is a large rock and a shrine is built on top of the rock. It is small in size and there is no permanent management staff, and unlike other shrines, it does not seem to be open all the time.

### [4.2.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#toc)Dangun statue

Usually, statues of great people are installed in schools or local governments with a close relationship with a particular great person. However, there are many cases where only the statue of Dangun is damaged. In particular, there are many cases where [Protestants](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B0%9C%EC%8B%A0%EA%B5%90/%EB%8C%80%ED%95%9C%EB%AF%BC%EA%B5%AD/%EC%82%AC%EA%B1%B4%EC%82%AC%EA%B3%A0/%EC%A2%85%EA%B5%90%EC%A0%81#s-28.3.2 "Protestantism/Korea/Incident/accident/religious") commit vandalism, because from the perspective of extreme Protestants, the statue of Dangun, who is worshipped as the ancestral god of the nation, is nothing more than an idol. In fact, extreme Protestants not only destroy the statue of Dangun, but also the Buddhist statues in temples.

The statue of Dangun, which was once actively installed, was erected by [Danworld](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EC%9B%94%EB%93%9C "Dan World") (formerly Danhak Seonwon), which is also very controversial. [#](http://www.donga.com/docs/magazine/new_donga/9912/nd99120420.html "http://www.donga.com/docs/magazine/new_donga/9912/nd99120420.html")

However, destroying the statue of Dangun, which was built by a religious group for the purpose of promoting their religion, is a crime that amounts to destruction of public facilities or infringement of private property. Since the Dangun Award was basically presented in the form of [donation](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B8%B0%EB%B6%80 "donation") to the school , the school owns it. Freedom of religion does not give you the right to take other people's property as you please.

In fact, if you want to remove the Dangun statue through a legal and normal procedure, there is a way to simply persuade the person or group that has the rights to the school property to remove the Dangun statue. Of course, those wishing for demolition will have to think for themselves about what kind of logic will be used to persuade them. If it is a private school, you can request it from the foundation. If it is a public school, the school principal has the authority, so if you ask the principal and they allow the removal, you can remove the Dangun statue completely legally. Requests made through the parents' association cannot be easily ignored by the chairman or principal, so it is best to persuade the school's parents' association. There are many Dangun statues that were legally removed in this way, and in cases where they were removed in this way, there is no problem, so it is not an issue.

The Protestants established the Dangunsang Problem Countermeasure Committee, which later developed into the Islamic Mission and Dangunsang Countermeasures Committee.

![Image 11](blob:http://localhost/5a63d274e2605325f6b8040bad97f110)![Image 12: File:external/pd...](https://i.namu.wiki/i/TE842Cd4P8EwkA9kOPA4mtq7Gyf5NRK2MRJmxUjG0Vm1cmOiLvmDrnWGqGnFVb2h_CTKkZ-ond51RpBB2yyPfLcI1JLvGZkwwHBypglVs4FDhSt2VM2hwoXg0c-iW3I45WhrnGs4OCzGcmYMaZLJlg.webp)

[North Korea](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%B6%81%ED%95%9C "North Korea") claims that [the Goguryeo](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%A0%EA%B5%AC%EB%A0%A4 "Goguryeo") -style tomb located in [Pyongyang](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%8F%89%EC%96%91 "Pyongyang") , excavated [in 1993,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/1993%EB%85%84 "1993") is the Tomb of Dangun. North Korea claims that this is because it was restored during the Goguryeo period. Since the location of Dangun's Tomb is in North Korea, confirmation must wait until unification, but since it is an independent investigation by [North Korea](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%B6%81%ED%95%9C "North Korea") , the historical academia, including in Korea, is skeptical.

The basis for North Korea's claim that it is Dangun's tomb is the radiometric dating of the excavated bones, but there are many differing opinions on this. And Pyongyang is used for regime propaganda, saying it has been the center since the Dangun era. Until then, North Korea's theory about the center of Gojoseon was point-centered. It is said that the theory changed to Pyongyang-centered after the discovery of Dangun's Tomb in Pyongyang, but since Dangun's Tomb itself is skeptical, there are many speculations about the background.

Relations with [China](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A4%91%EA%B5%AD "china") , system stabilization, etc. In other words, it can be assumed that the theory did not change through the excavation of Dangun's tomb, but that Dangun's tomb was created because there was a need to change the theory. For reference, there is a claim that the founder of North Korea, 'Kim Il-sung = Dangun', and the second generation 'Kim Jong-il = Wang Geon' (the leading figure of unification) were trying to brainwash the people.

[6.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#toc)[standard portrait](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%91%9C%EC%A4%80%EC%98%81%EC%A0%95 "government standard portrait")
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Under the leadership of [the Park Chung-hee](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%B0%95%EC%A0%95%ED%9D%AC "Park Chung-hee") government, standard portraits were designated for all Korean historical figures, and of course, the portraits of Dangun were also newly drawn. In 1978, it was commissioned by artist Hong Sook-ho and painted. In simple terms, **it is a nationally recognized portrait of Dangun** .

However, since it is a modern [creation](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%B0%BD%EC%9E%91%EB%AC%BC "creations") , it has no great historical significance.[[30]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#fn-30 "Of course, the paintings depicting Dangun in the past are at most the same as the works of the late Joseon Dynasty.") The standard portrait itself, which has entered the present, has many problems and is often criticized, so it is not used as much as before.

Unlike the portraits of Dangun before the 1970s, which were decorated with various leaves, such decorations have disappeared.

In addition, there are several pictures. Some are written in Daejonggyo, some are written in Samseongsa Temple in Hwanghae-do, some are written by Kim Jong-rae, and some are written by Hong Seok-chang in Hyeonjeonghoe.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-3) Mythology Before 2333 BC[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-4) 1900 Commemoration of King Gojong of the Korean Empire.[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-5) It is 1048 in 《 [Jewangungi](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A0%9C%EC%99%95%EC%9A%B4%EA%B8%B0 "emperor luck") 》.[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-6) It is a record that is presumed to be a combination of the reigns of all Danguns (presumed) of Gojoseon, not just the first Dangun, or it is still unclear. Details below.[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-7) Dangun means religious ruler (priest).[[8]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-8) Wanggeom refers to a political ruler.[[9]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-9) In 《 [Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms](https://db.history.go.kr/item/level.do?sort=levelId&dir=ASC&start=1&limit=20&page=1&pre_page=1&setId=1&totalCount=1&prevPage=0&prevLimit=&itemId=sy&types=r&synonym=off&chinessChar=on&brokerPagingInfo=&levelId=sy_001r_0020_0150_0020&position=0 "https://db.history.go.kr/item/level.do?sort=levelId&dir=ASC&start=1&limit=20&page=1&pre_page=1&setId=1&totalCount=1&prevPage=0&prevLimit=&itemId=sy&types=r&synonym=off&chinessChar=on&brokerPagingInfo=&levelId=sy_001r_0020_0150_0020&position=0") 》, he appears as the same person as [Mrs. Yuhwa](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9C%A0%ED%99%94%EB%B6%80%EC%9D%B8 "Mrs. Yuhwa") .[[10]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-10) King Haeburu[[11]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-11) King Chumo[[12]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-12) This is the height of the remains claimed to be the remains of Dangun found in [the Dangunneung](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EB%A6%89 "Tomb of Dangun") . However, considering that the person buried in the tomb of Dangun in South Korea is presumed to be a local Goguryeo nobleman, not Dangun, it is highly likely that it is the height of a Goguryeo local nobleman buried in the tomb, not Dangun's [height](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EB%A6%89 "Tomb of Dangun") .[[13]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-13) ( [Example: 2nd Dangun - 3rd Dangun...)](https://terms.naver.com/entry.nhn?docId=985922&cid=47322&categoryId=47322 "https://terms.naver.com/entry.nhn?docId=985922&cid=47322&categoryId=47322")[[14]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-14) Through this, it can be interpreted that Dangun Wanggeom has the meaning of " [the king of the sky](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%B2%9C%EC%8B%A0 "angel") ."[[15]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-15) It is customary to capitalize the first syllable to indicate that it is taken from medieval Korean rather than from a recorded ancient pronunciation.[[16]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-16) In fact, it is unclear whether among the books Il-yeon quoted, there is a book titled 《Gogi》, or whether it just means an old record (Gogi, Gogi). However, until the early Joseon Dynasty, many books related to meat were extant, and it is quoted in many books, so it is difficult to know what their contents are. However, sadly, it was not fully transmitted to posterity because the narrative content or exaggerated content occupied a large part.[[17]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-17) During the Joseon Dynasty, when envoys from China (Myeong) came, it was natural for them to come in the order of Uiju→Pyongyang→Hanseong (Seoul). This is until the Yeongmyojo (Sejong Dynasty) in the early Joseon Dynasty.[[18]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-18) As will be explained below, the age of the myth of Dangun itself was determined in the following way: ① Dangun was a figure contemporaneous with Liao in China → ② Recognized the historical existence of Liao as fact and determined the age → ③ Defined the historical age of Dangun [.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9A%94(%EC%82%BC%ED%99%A9%EC%98%A4%EC%A0%9C) "Yo (Three Emperors and Five Emperors)") However, since the modern times , it is not clear whether even Hana, let alone King Yao, [can](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%98%EB%82%98%EB%9D%BC "one ra") be recognized as fact, so the link of logic itself has been cut off. Nonetheless, those who claim that the myth of Dangun is true hold a double standard, believing in the date of 2333 B.C. However, those who are truly Hwanpa generally affirm the Three Emperors and Five Emperors and only interpret them in favor of Korea.[[19]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-19) However, it is difficult to see it as a double standard because the part related to the wage may have been added later. It is highly probable that oral legends from the Bronze Age or the Gojoseon Period continued to be handed down in the Pyongyang area, and that the details related to the wages of Yao were added to later generations for reasons such as increasing reliability through the presentation of specific dates or instilling national pride that is not inferior to China. Originally, literature such as oral legends, tales, and legends are characterized by gaining weight over time.[[20]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-20) An annotated text that recorded and annotated the rites of sacrifice.[[21]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-21) In Goryeosa, there is a record that the Goryeo government held a rite every season by lowering the pressure in Dongmyeongseongjesa, and Pyongyang officials held ancestral rites on the 1st and 15th of every [month](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8F%99%EB%AA%85%EC%84%B1%EC%99%95 "King Dongmyeongseong") . You can see that it was bigger than worship.[[22]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-22) This contrasts with the Samguk sagi, which was produced in the middle of the Goryeo Dynasty, which did not include the records of Dangun at all. There is a record of 'seonin wanggeom', but it is unknown whether the seonin wanggeom is Dangun.[[23]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-23) At this time, Kija was enshrined separately in [Sunginjeon,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%88%AD%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%84 "숭인전") but King Dongmyeongseong was enshrined together in Sungnyeongjeon. As [Haemosu](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%B4%EB%AA%A8%EC%88%98 "Haemosu") was identified with Dangun, it is assumed that King Dongmyeongseong was treated as Dangun's son.[[24]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-24) Originally, however, mortuary tablets and wooden statues were enshrined together, but King Taejong’s great chancellor Ha Ryun [suggested](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%95%98%EB%A5%9C "lower wheel") destroying the wooden statues enshrined in shrines across the country and enshrining only the ancestral tablets, so the wooden statues disappeared and only the ancestral tablets remained in Samseongsa. This wooden statue does not appear to have been restored.[[25]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-25) During the Korean Empire, it was elevated to [the Tomb of Dangun](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EB%A6%89 "Tomb of Dangun") .[[26]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-26) In addition, because [Wiman](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9C%84%EB%A7%8C "stomach only") was a usurper who dared to harm Dangun's legitimacy, his status fell to the bottom and he was extremely despised.[[27]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-27) For reference, many people misunderstand, but it is Hwanin, not Dangun, who is revered as the main god in [Daejonggyo](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8 "Hwanin") .[[28]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-28) It does not appear in the Samguk Sagi magazine, Jiri.[[29]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-29) The Dangun Shrine moved to Pyongyang is [Sungnyeongjeon](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%88%AD%EB%A0%B9%EC%A0%84 "Sungnyeongjeon") in Pyongyang .[[30]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-30) Of course, the paintings depicting Dangun in the past are at most the same as the works of the late Joseon Dynasty.[[31]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-31) As a similar example, in [Japan](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%BC%EB%B3%B8 "japan")[, Izanagi,](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%B4%EC%9E%90%EB%82%98%EA%B8%B0 "Izanagi") the creator god of [Japanese mythology](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%9D%BC%EB%B3%B8%20%EC%8B%A0%ED%99%94 "japanese mythology") , is used in the same way. Representatively, there is the Izanagi game, which is the most booming period in Japanese history and was [during the Leeds era](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%A6%AC%EC%A6%88%EC%8B%9C%EC%A0%88 "리즈시절") . Originally, this was called the 'Jimmu game' because the boom caused by economic growth in the first half of the 1950s was the biggest boom since Emperor Jimmu, but as the boom continued in the late 1950s, it [appeared](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%A7%84%EB%AC%B4%20%EC%B2%9C%ED%99%A9 "Emperor Jimmu") in the mythology of the god in the sense of the biggest since [Amaterasu Okami.](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%95%84%EB%A7%88%ED%85%8C%EB%9D%BC%EC%8A%A4 "Amaterasu") After calling it the "Iwato Match," it was called the "Izanagi Match," which dates back even further in the 1960s.[[32]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A8%EA%B5%B0%EC%99%95%EA%B2%80#rfn-32) However , it was later revealed that Israel produces quite a lot of [shale gas](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%85%B0%EC%9D%BC%EA%B0%80%EC%8A%A4 "shale gas") .
